action: Woolworths urges customers who see e-gift card transactions they do not recognise to contact its Gift Card Support team or report them through the Everyday Gifting website.

evidence.quote: Shoppers have reported losses of up to $500, with some discovering their gift cards had been completely emptied

exec: Gift card fraud at Woolworths with no stated cause; the company is reimbursing affected customers with replacement cards.
plain: Dozens of Woolworths shoppers found their digital gift cards had been spent by someone else. Woolworths apologised and is issuing replacement cards; the reports do not say what caused it.
summary: An ABC News investigation published November 16 found dozens of customers whose digital WISH gift cards were emptied by transactions they did not make, with losses of up to $500. Woolworths apologised and, Sunrise reported on November 17, has begun issuing replacement gift cards so affected customers are fully reimbursed. Neither report says how card details were obtained or whether a cyberattack occurred; nothing links it to the Coles incident.
title: Woolworths acknowledges issue after customers report drained digital gift cards

validation.note: The Cyber Express (relaying ABC News) and The Nightly (republishing Sunrise, 17 Nov) each report the drained cards and quote Woolworths' acknowledgement; The Nightly also quotes its apology and the replacement cards. Neither gives a cause.

review.note: Compared ABC investigation of 16 Nov, dozens of customers, up to $500, Woolworths acknowledgement, cause unknown, no Coles link against The Cyber Express; status developing.
